comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C152-C162 regarding broader mechanistic insights and generalization across pLGICs. Both evaluations affirm that the findings extend beyond 5-HT3R to the broader receptor family, with reviewers explicitly supporting the comparative analysis and conservation of activation mechanisms.

Strong agreement on claims C130-C136 regarding pre-active state annotation. Both evaluations support the structural assignment of intermediate conformations to pre-active states, with integration of SCAM data and recent cryo-EM structures. Reviewers accept this functional annotation without challenge.

Full agreement on claims C40-C46 regarding kinetic properties and temporal separation of activation and desensitization. Both evaluations treat the stable fluorescence during desensitization as a methodological strength that validates the focus on activation-related conformational changes.

Agreement on claims C72-C75 characterizing the I160C/Y207W sensor loss-of-function phenotype. Both evaluations accept this characterization as part of the systematic analysis, with reviewers treating the phenotype as useful for revealing intermediate states.

Agreement on claims C82-C85 regarding vestibular and ECD-TMD sensor phenotypes. Both evaluations accept the gain-of-function characterization and N101K reversion as demonstrating allosteric coupling, with no concerns raised about these findings.

Strong agreement on claims C115-C119 regarding the concerted mechanism for strong agonists. Both evaluations support the correlation between fluorescence and current, with reviewers treating this as a well-established result that is convincing and rigorous.

Full agreement on claims C47-C51, C102-C104 regarding antagonist effects and localized conformational changes. Both evaluations strongly affirm the finding that setrons produce conformational changes at the orthosteric site but fail to propagate to lower ECD regions, validating the inhibition mechanism.

Agreement on claims C52-C56 regarding S204C sensor pharmacological characterization. Both evaluations accept the EC50 and efficacy data without challenge, treating the demonstration that sensors don't perturb function as validation of the approach.

Agreement on claims C95-C101 regarding comparative analysis with other pLGICs and methodological innovation. Both evaluations accept the tryptophan-induced quenching approach and comparisons with h5-HT3AR and α1-GlyR, with reviewers implicitly affirming the technical success.

Strong agreement on claims C34, C36-C37, C93-C94, C100 regarding successful sensor development and screening. Both evaluations affirm the convincing investigation of structural changes inside and outside the orthosteric site, with reviewers explicitly supporting the sensor design approach.

Agreement on claims C147-C150 regarding the four-state model and consistency with structural data. Both evaluations support the functional annotation of cryo-EM structures, with reviewers noting the results correlate well with structural observations and help annotate existing structures.

Agreement on claims C105, C107-C108, C111-C114 regarding integration of VCF data with cryo-EM structures. Both evaluations support the consistency between fluorescence patterns and conformational changes, with reviewers affirming the validation of setron-inhibited structures.

Both evaluations acknowledge uncertainty regarding claims C141-C142 about orthosteric sensor interpretation. OpenEval notes the inability to distinguish between setron-like and pre-active conformations, while reviewers highlight the incomplete TMD annotation as a remaining limitation.

Strong agreement on claims C120-C128 regarding intermediate conformations and pre-active states. Both evaluations treat this as a key mechanistic insight, with reviewers highlighting the decorrelation of fluorescence and current in loss-of-function mutants as strong evidence for intermediates.

Agreement on claims C64-C71 regarding N101K mutation effects and decorrelation of fluorescence and current. Both evaluations support this as evidence for intermediate conformations, with reviewers emphasizing the stabilization of intermediate states in mutant conditions.

Agreement on abstract claims C7-C8 regarding four conformational families and consistency with cryo-EM. Both evaluations support these summary findings, with reviewers affirming the correlation with structural data and functional annotation contribution.

Agreement on claim C167 regarding future utility of the sensors. Both evaluations affirm the prospective value for drug characterization and further studies, with reviewers noting interest for channel biophysics and drug development communities.

Agreement on claims C86, C91 regarding concerted mechanism for strong agonists at vestibular sensors. Both evaluations support this finding as part of the broader evidence for concerted activation, with reviewers treating the experiments as rigorous and convincing.

Agreement on claim C33 regarding the VCF experimental approach. Both evaluations support the methodology, with reviewers affirming the successful application to investigate conformational changes at multiple receptor sites.

Partial overlap on claims C76-C78 regarding three-state model synthesis. OpenEval focuses on the orthosteric sensor data supporting the model, while peer reviewers emphasize the broader evidence for intermediate states including these findings as part of the overall mechanistic picture.

Agreement on abstract claim C6 regarding four sensor development. Both evaluations affirm the successful creation of sensors at two positions inside and two outside the agonist binding site, treating this as a foundational achievement.

Agreement on abstract claim C9 regarding differential effects of strong vs. partial agonists. Both evaluations support this finding, with reviewers treating the distinction as well-established through the rigorous experimental approach.

Agreement on claims C60-C61 regarding varenicline revealing intermediate conformations at S204C. Both evaluations support this as early evidence for intermediates, with reviewers emphasizing this as part of the broader finding about partial agonist-stabilized states.

Partial overlap on claims C138-C139 regarding intermediate conformations at orthosteric sensors. OpenEval acknowledges interpretive challenges, while peer reviewers incorporate these observations into the broader supported finding about intermediate states without highlighting the ambiguity.

OpenEval supports claims C1-C3, C11-C15 regarding established 5-HT3R knowledge and background context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate background/contextual claims.

OpenEval supports claims C4-C5, C19-C30 regarding prior structural work and knowledge gaps. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately assess the literature review establishing the study's motivation.

OpenEval supports claims C16-C18 regarding established pLGIC mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate mechanistic background claims providing context for VCF experiments.

OpenEval supports claims C31-C32 regarding VCF technique description and prior applications. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately assess methodological background beyond the current application.

Minimal overlap on claim C165 regarding VCF approach significance. OpenEval groups this with other summary claims, while peer reviewers mention the validation of setron mechanism as part of the antagonist findings rather than as a separate significance statement.

Minimal overlap on claim C145 regarding progressive signal propagation. OpenEval includes this in the four-state model synthesis, while peer reviewers address intermediate states more broadly without specifically highlighting the progressive propagation pattern.
